what: cs-thm-certsel / cs-cor-menu(ii) instrumented on the Darcy rung: the certification split DRAWN fresh from the reference flow and swept in L2, so the deliverable is the curve of certification rate against certification budget.

protocol.reference: rho_y = the trained conditional flow (darcy_stuart_npe run e9ba2c58df), a samplable measure. Certification draws are FRESH draws from it.
protocol.arms: reproduced from dq_darcy_stuart._evaluate: bank size bank_L (2x at M >= 256), generator base_seed + 50_000 + 1000*M + obs, seeds WITH replacement, deduped with multiplicity, weights from the unit-sum constrained solve against that bank.
protocol.certification_seed_rule: base_seed + 610000 + obs -- a data-independent offset. No estimand-bank atom, arm, or network parameter reaches the stream.
protocol.independence: the split shares no draw with any estimand bank, the network never saw this observation, and the bandwidth is a functional of the TRAINING observations' draws -- so every quantity used to fit or score the arms is independent of the split, which is the theorem's hypothesis.
protocol.what_the_certificate_does_NOT_repair: the seeds are rows of the estimand bank (the rung's own convention), so they are i.i.d. draws of the bank's empirical measure rather than of rho, and the arms carry e2-prop-overlap's shrinkage. cs-thm-certsel is indifferent to how the arms were produced -- it needs only that the split is independent of them -- so the certificate is valid AND certifies the rule as fitted, shrinkage included. It does not launder the fit; it prices the comparison.
protocol.rho_is_the_flow: MMD^2 in the certificate is against the FLOW, not against a bank: the split is drawn from the flow, so the guarantee is 'never worse than its seeds as an integrator of rho_y'. The rung's own reported depths are against the bank-as-measure, a different and weaker object.
protocol.l2_grid_is_nested: the grid's smaller budgets are exact prefix checkpoints of one stream (verified bit-identical against a single call), so the whole curve costs one pass.
protocol.selection: TWO selections are certified: (a) argmin of Jhat on the split over the live three-arm menu -- cs-cor-menu(ii), each pair at delta/3 under cs-eq-gammahat's own ln(4/.) numerator; and (b) the DEPLOYED argmin on the fitting estimand, which is what the rung actually emits and is equally independent of the split.
protocol.simultaneity_disclosure: cs-thm-certsel prices ONE emission against ONE split. This sweep reuses each observation's split across every redraw and budget, so each cell's verdict is a valid MARGINAL 1-delta statement and the reported rate is an average of marginal certificates, not a simultaneous statement over the cells sharing a split. The Bonferroni slack that would make it simultaneous over one split's whole service is reported as gamma_hat_simultaneous / rate_simultaneous.
protocol.bandwidth: read from the trained run's results.json, never recomputed from anything scored here.

draw_ledger.currency: reference draws consumed per observation -- the same ledger sec 6.3 prices the compression peers against.
draw_ledger.note: the split is DRAWN from the flow, not carved out of the estimand bank, so certification costs the arms no precision at all: the estimand bank is untouched and every number the rung already reports is unmoved. What it costs is draws, plus O(M L2) kernel evaluations to contract them. For reference the rung's own per-observation estimand bank is 8192 draws (16384 at the two deepest budgets).
draw_ledger.one_split_serves: one drawn split serves every budget and every redraw at its observation, so the per-observation draw cost is paid ONCE for all of them -- but see the simultaneity disclosure: the marginal per-emission verdict is what that reuse licenses, and the Bonferroni column is what would license the joint statement.

arm_identity.note: the median over this run's observation subsample against the shipped run's 64-observation median and interquartile band. The shipped record stores no per-observation values and its flow sampling may have run in float32 on the GPU, so band containment is the strongest statement available -- not a bitwise identity claim, which the record cannot support.
